title: Source Water, Salts and Contaminant Risk

content.overview: A water source is more than pH and EC. Wells, municipal water, reclaimed water and captured water can differ in alkalinity, sodium/chloride, hardness, nutrients, microbial load and trace contaminants. Suitability depends on source history, crop use and applicable quality requirements.

vocabulary.definition: Measurement and documentation used to understand the chemical and microbiological properties of a water source.
Total effect of dissolved salts that can influence osmotic conditions and crop response.
A chemical or biological constituent whose presence or concentration may create crop, worker, product or regulatory concern.

sections.title: EC is a screening measurement, not a contaminant panel
sections.body: EC reflects bulk ionic conductivity but cannot identify which salts or trace contaminants are present. Major-ion and risk-based testing may be needed when source composition matters.

sections.title: Reclaimed water requires ongoing verification
sections.body: A 2026 outdoor cannabis study using reclaimed municipal wastewater found several measured quality indicators acceptable and no systematic accumulation of many metals, yet lead in dried flowers exceeded referenced regulatory limits. The result supports monitoring rather than assuming source safety from general water chemistry alone.

sections.title: Source changes should trigger review
sections.body: Season, well conditions, treatment changes or blending can change water composition. Preserve sample date, source and treatment state with results.

workedExamples: Two waters with the same EC can differ substantially in sodium, calcium, bicarbonate or other constituents.
A reclaimed-water program should not rely on one historical lab report if treatment or source conditions change.
commonMistakes: Calling water safe because pH and EC look normal.
Ignoring source history and treatment changes.
Using one test panel for every possible source risk.
content.practicalApplication: Create a source-water specification with routine pH/EC/alkalinity and a risk-based panel for major ions, microbiology or trace contaminants depending on source and use.
content.summary: Advanced source-water management combines basic chemistry with source-specific contamination risk and repeated verification.
